title_en: Mai Liang's Application for State Compensation
ruling_gist_en: The acceptance of a compensation application occurred before the amendment of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, while the compensation decision was made after the amendment. The application of law in such a case should be determined in accordance with the Legislation Law of the People's Republic of China. Article 84 of the Legislation Law provides that laws shall not be retroactive, except for special provisions made to better protect the rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations. The amended State Compensation Law provides greater protection for the rights and interests of compensation claimants. The Judicial Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the State Compensation Law also clearly stipulates that if a compensation request was accepted before December 1, 2010, and no effective compensation decision has been made by December 1, 2010, the amended State Compensation Law shall apply. Therefore, such cases shall be governed by the amended State Compensation Law.

full_text_en:
Mai Liang v. Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Court and Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Procuratorate — dispute over state compensation

Ruling Summary

Where an application for compensation is accepted prior to the amendment of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, but the compensation decision is rendered after the amendment, the applicable law shall be determined in accordance with the Legislation Law of the People's Republic of China. Article 84 of the Legislation Law provides that a law shall not have retroactive effect, except for special provisions made to better protect the rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations. The amended State Compensation Law provides stronger protection for the rights and interests of compensation claimants. The judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the application of the State Compensation Law also clearly provides that where a compensation claim is accepted before December 1, 2010, but no effective compensation decision has been made by December 1, 2010, the amended State Compensation Law shall apply. Therefore, in such circumstances, the amended State Compensation Law shall be applied.

Claimant for Compensation: Mai Liang, male, 47 years old, Han Chinese, residing at Jinbi Huafu, Zhujiang New Town, Guangzhou.

Respondent: Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Court, domiciled at Longkou West Road, Dahe District, Guangzhou.
Legal Representative: Gan Zhengpei, President of the court.

Respondent: Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Procuratorate, domiciled at Longkou West Road, Tianhe District, Guangzhou.
Legal Representative: Zhang Zhiqiang, Chief Procurator of the procuratorate.

Claimant Mai Liang, in a case concerning erroneous arrest and erroneous judgment, being dissatisfied with the Joint Compensation Decision (2010) Tian Fa Pei Zi No. 1 rendered by the Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Court (hereinafter "Tianhe District Court") and the Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Procuratorate (hereinafter "Tianhe District Procuratorate") on November 5, 2010, applied to the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter "Guangzhou Intermediate Court") on November 15, 2010 for a compensation decision.

Claimant Mai Liang alleged: On March 15, 2007, the Tianhe District Procuratorate detained him on suspicion of dereliction of duty, and he was not acquitted until November 5, 2009, when the Guangzhou Intermediate Court rendered a verdict of not guilty, a period of two years and eight months. During this prolonged ordeal, he suffered great harm to his physical health, mental state, and even his family and career. He frequently suffers from headaches and insomnia, his vision and memory have declined, his wife has developed schizophrenia, and his son was unable to gain admission to a better university in 2007. The two Respondents' decision to compensate him in the amount of RMB 74,003.70 is clearly insufficient to redress the harm he has suffered. Additionally, he strongly requests that the relevant authorities investigate the cause of this case, specifically the truth of the conspiracy by personnel of the Guangdong Provincial Sports Bureau and the Guangdong Provincial Sports Lottery Management Center to fabricate information and collude with judicial personnel to persecute him, and to pursue the legal liability of those responsible in accordance with the law. Requests: 1. The Respondents shall pay compensation for the infringement of his personal freedom; 2. The Respondents shall pay damages for the harm caused to his physical health; 3. The Respondents shall eliminate the effects, restore his reputation, and apologize to him, and pay moral damages and compensation for the impact on his political future; 4. The Respondents shall pay compensation for the physical and mental harm suffered by his family members; 5. The Guangdong Provincial Sports Bureau shall be ordered to retroactively pay his wages, subsidies, etc., totaling RMB 11 million for the above five items; 6. Legal liability shall be pursued against personnel of the Guangdong Provincial Sports Bureau and the Guangdong Provincial Sports Lottery Management Center who abused their power to bring false charges and engage in framing, as well as against the judicial personnel of the relevant authorities who caused the unjust and erroneous case.

Respondent Tianhe District Court stated: The case of claimant Mai Liang has been lawfully reversed and an acquittal entered by the Guangzhou Intermediate Court through legal procedures. Pursuant to the 1994 State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, where a court of first instance renders a guilty verdict but the court of second instance reverses the verdict and finds the defendant not guilty, compensation shall be jointly paid by the court of first instance and the procuratorate that initiated the public prosecution. The content and scope of compensation, in accordance with the 1994 State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, shall be calculated based on the national average daily wage of employees in the previous year, compensating Mai Liang for the period from the date of his detention to the date of his release on bail pending trial, totaling RMB 74,003.70. Regarding compensation for physical injury to the claimant and the elimination of effects, restoration of reputation, apology, and payment of moral damages, under the 1994 State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, a legal causal relationship must exist; otherwise, no compensation shall be paid. Mai Liang's case underwent investigation, public prosecution, and trial. If the claimant suffered some degree of infringement on his personal rights and right to reputation, compensation should be paid according to the different responsible entities. The court has paid compensation for the infringement of personal freedom during the period of detention in accordance with the law. The other compensation requested by the claimant (compensation for impact on political future, compensation for family members, moral damages, etc.) does not fall within the scope of state compensation and shall not be paid.

Respondent Tianhe District Procuratorate did not state any opinion.

The Compensation Committee of the Guangzhou Intermediate Court, upon trial, found that the claimant Mai Liang was criminally detained by the Tianhe Branch of the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau on March 14, 2007, on suspicion of dereliction of duty (Mai Liang was admitted to the Tianhe District Detention Center on the same day and signed the detention warrant at 1:00 a.m. on March 15, 2007). He was arrested on March 29, 2007, upon approval by the Tianhe District Procuratorate, and was taken into custody on the same day. On August 6, 2007, the Tianhe District Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against Mai Liang for dereliction of duty in the Tianhe District Court. On February 2, 2008, the Tianhe District Court rendered the criminal judgment (2007) Tian Fa Xing Chu Zi No. 1150, finding Mai Liang guilty of dereliction of duty and sentencing him to three years and six months of imprisonment. Mai Liang appealed. On July 17, 2008, the Guangzhou Intermediate Court rendered the criminal ruling (2008) Sui Zhong Fa Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 182, quashing the original judgment and remanding the case to the Tianhe District Court for retrial. On October 24, 2008, the Tianhe District Court decided to release Mai Liang on bail pending trial. On February 16, 2009, the Tianhe District Court rendered the criminal judgment (2008) Tian Fa Xing Chong Zi No. 7, finding Mai Liang guilty of dereliction of duty but exempting him from criminal punishment. Both the Tianhe District Procuratorate and Mai Liang appealed, with the procuratorate filing a protest and Mai Liang filing an appeal to the Guangzhou Intermediate Court. On November 5, 2009, the Guangzhou Intermediate Court rendered the criminal judgment (2009) Sui Zhong Fa Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 204, finding Mai Liang not guilty due to insufficient evidence.

On October 19, 2010, claimant Mai Liang applied to the Tianhe District Court and the Tianhe District Procuratorate for compensation on the grounds that the erroneous detention, arrest, and trial had caused him harm. On November 5, 2010, the Tianhe District Court and the Tianhe District Procuratorate rendered the Joint Compensation Decision (2010) Tian Fa Pei Zi No. 1, determining that Mai Liang had been detained for a total of 590 days, from March 15, 2007, when he was criminally detained, to October 24, 2008, when he was released on bail pending trial. The decision awarded Mai Liang compensation of RMB 74,003.70. The Tianhe District Court and the Tianhe District Procuratorate were designated as joint Respondents, each bearing RMB 37,001.85 of the compensation. Mai Liang, dissatisfied, applied to the Compensation Committee of the Guangzhou Intermediate Court for a compensation decision.

It was additionally found that the claimant Mai Liang was detained for a total of 591 days, from March 14, 2007, when he was admitted to the Tianhe District Detention Center, to October 24, 2008, when he was released on bail pending trial.

The focus of the dispute in this application for state compensation was whether the other compensation requests made by claimant Mai Liang, aside from compensation for infringement of personal freedom, have a legal basis.

On December 20, 2010, the Guangzhou Intermediate Court rendered the Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1. The decision held that, pursuant to Article 15 of the 1994 State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, where an organ exercising procuratorial or adjudicative powers erroneously arrests a person who has no criminal facts, the victim has the right to obtain compensation. Paragraph 1 of Article 20 provides that a Respondent shall pay compensation when the existence of one of the circumstances specified in Article 15 of this Law has been lawfully confirmed. Article 26 provides that the daily compensation for infringement of a citizen's personal freedom shall be calculated based on the national average daily wage of employees in the previous year. Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Joint Compensation by People's Courts and People's Procuratorates provides that, where a procuratorate approves an arrest and initiates a public prosecution, the court of first instance renders a guilty verdict, and the court of second instance reverses the verdict and finds the defendant not guilty, the court of first instance and the procuratorate that approved the arrest shall be the joint Respondents. Article 3 provides that, in an acquittal case where the court of second instance declares the defendant not guilty, the people's court and the people's procuratorate serving as joint Respondents shall each bear one-half of the compensation amount. In this case, the Tianhe District Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution in the Tianhe District Court, charging claimant Mai Liang with dereliction of duty. The Tianhe District Court rendered a guilty verdict at first instance, but the court of second instance reversed the verdict and found him not guilty due to insufficient evidence. The criminal judgment (2009) Sui Zhong Fa Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 204 declaring Mai Liang not guilty constitutes confirmation of the erroneous arrest of Mai Liang. In accordance with the above provisions, Mai Liang has the right to obtain compensation, and the Tianhe District Court and the Tianhe District Procuratorate shall be the joint Respondents. The national average daily wage of employees in 2009 was RMB 125.43 per day, and Mai Liang did not object to this standard. Regarding the number of days of detention, upon review, the Tianhe Branch of the Guangzhou Public Security Bureau issued a detention warrant on March 14, 2007, to execute the detention of Mai Liang, and Mai Liang was admitted to the Tianhe District Detention Center on that same day. Mai Liang's claim that the period of detention was 591 days is well-founded. The calculation by the two Respondents of 590 days of erroneous detention, starting from March 15, 2007, was erroneous and should be corrected. Therefore, the total compensation for infringement of personal freedom payable by the two Respondents to Mai Liang is RMB 74,129.13 (RMB 125.43 × 591 days), with each Respondent bearing one-half of the compensation liability.

Regarding the request of claimant Mai Liang for compensation for physical injury, Mai Liang failed to provide evidence proving that the Respondents committed an act infringing upon his right to life and health and that such act had been confirmed as unlawful. Therefore, this request is not supported.

Regarding the request of claimant Mai Liang for the Respondents to pay moral damages, the 1994 State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China does not contain provisions regarding "payment of moral damages." Therefore, Mai Liang's request in this regard has no legal basis and is not supported.

The requests of claimant Mai Liang for the Respondents to pay compensation for the physical and mental injury suffered by his family members, for the Guangdong Provincial Sports Bureau to be ordered to retroactively pay his wages and bonuses, and for the pursuit of legal liability against those responsible, do not fall within the scope of compensation provided for by the State Compensation Law and are also not supported.

Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 15 and 26 of the 1994 State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, the Compensation Committee of the Guangzhou Intermediate Court decided on December 20, 2010:

1. To quash the Joint Compensation Decision (2010) Tian Fa Pei Zi No. 1 rendered by the Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Court and the Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Procuratorate on November 5, 2010;

2. The Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Court and the Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Procuratorate shall pay the claimant Mai Liang compensation for infringement of personal freedom in the amount of RMB 74,129.13, with each organ bearing RMB 37,064.57;

3. To dismiss the other compensation requests of the claimant Mai Liang.

Mai Liang, dissatisfied with the compensation decision of the Compensation Committee of the Guangzhou Intermediate Court, appealed to the Compensation Committee of the Guangdong High People's Court, contending: 1. The Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 erroneously avoided addressing his request that the Respondents be ordered to eliminate the effects, restore his reputation, and apologize to him, which is contrary to the provisions of the State Compensation Law. The appellant was erroneously arrested and erroneously found guilty of dereliction of duty, and was detained in a detention center for 591 days without cause, suffering great harm physically, mentally, and in terms of political impact. The State Compensation Law has explicit provisions on this matter; this request is justified and should be supported. 2. The Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 erroneously refused to support the appellant's request for compensation for physical injury on the grounds that "Mai Liang failed to provide evidence proving that the Respondents committed an act infringing upon his right to life and health and that such act had been confirmed as unlawful." The appellant was incarcerated for a long period, and the interrogations by the case-handling organs caused mental harm. The medical records and examination results of the appellant and his family members can prove this. The Respondents have already confirmed the error; the appellant only needs to prove that he suffered physical harm to be entitled to compensation, and need not further obtain separate confirmation of unlawfulness from the Respondents. 3. The Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 was rendered after the amendment of the State Compensation Law. The amended State Compensation Law added compensation for moral damages. The appellant's request for payment of moral damages should be supported. In summary, he requests that the Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 be quashed and that all the requests made in his application for state compensation be supported.

The Compensation Committee of the Guangdong High People's Court found the facts upon trial to be consistent with those found by the Compensation Committee of the Guangzhou Intermediate Court.

The focus of the dispute during the appeal period was whether the amended State Compensation Law can be applied where the compensation application was accepted before the amendment of the State Compensation Law, but the compensation decision was rendered after the amendment and before the issuance of the judicial interpretation.

The Compensation Committee of the Guangdong High People's Court held that, regarding the applicable law in this case, the amended State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China came into effect on December 1, 2010. The appellant Mai Liang was detained from 2007 to 2008, applied to the Guangzhou Intermediate Court for a compensation decision on November 15, 2010, and the Guangzhou Intermediate Court rendered the Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 on December 20, 2010. Since there was no relevant judicial interpretation at that time providing for the application of the State Compensation Law before and after its amendment, the Guangzhou Intermediate Court, in accordance with the general principle that laws do not have retroactive effect, applied the law in effect at the time of the conduct, i.e., the 1994 State Compensation Law. During the review of this appeal, the Supreme People's Court, on February 14, 2011, adopted the Interpretation (I) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 2 of which provides: "Where an act committed by a state organ or its personnel in exercising their functions and powers infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a citizen, legal person, or other organization before December 1, 2010, the pre-amendment State Compensation Law shall apply, except in the following circumstances where the amended State Compensation Law shall apply: ... (1) Where a compensation request has been accepted before December 1, 2010, but no effective compensation decision has been made by December 1, 2010; ..." Given that the Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 was rendered on December 20, 2010, it falls within the above circumstance, and therefore the amended State Compensation Law shall now apply to this case.

In this case, the appellant Mai Liang was detained from March 14, 2007, to October 24, 2008, when he was released on bail pending trial, for a total of 591 days. The Tianhe District Court rendered a guilty verdict at first instance, and the Guangzhou Intermediate Court reversed the verdict and found Mai Liang not guilty at second instance. Pursuant to the new provision of Paragraph 4 of Article 21 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, where a court of second instance reverses a guilty verdict and finds the defendant not guilty, the people's court that rendered the guilty verdict at first instance shall be the Respondent. Therefore, the Respondent in this case is the Tianhe District Court. The Tianhe District Court shall, in accordance with Articles 17, 22, and 33 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, compensate Mai Liang with corresponding compensation for infringement of personal freedom in the amount of RMB 74,129.13 (RMB 125.43/day × 591 days).

After the appellant Mai Liang was detained, relevant media reported the matter, causing serious damage to Mai Liang's reputation. The psychological outpatient report made after Mai Liang was released on bail pending trial showed that he had (mild) depressive symptoms. Article 35 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where any of the circumstances specified in Article 3 or Article 17 of this Law causes mental harm, the effects shall be eliminated, the reputation restored, and an apology made to the victim within the scope of the impact of the infringing act; where serious consequences are caused, corresponding moral damages shall be paid." Therefore, the Respondent, the Tianhe District Court, shall, within the scope of the impact of the infringing act, eliminate the effects for Mai Liang, restore his reputation, apologize to him, and pay Mai Liang corresponding moral damages. This appeal by Mai Liang is in accordance with the law and should be supported. Considering the specific circumstances of this case, the Respondent is ordered to pay Mai Liang RMB 50,000 in moral damages.

Regarding the request of the appellant Mai Liang that the Respondents pay damages for infringing upon his physical health, upon examination, Mai Liang failed to provide evidence proving that the Respondents committed an act infringing upon his right to life and health, and therefore this request is not supported.

Regarding the requests of the appellant Mai Liang that the Respondents pay compensation for the physical and mental injury suffered by his family members, that the Guangdong Provincial Sports Bureau be ordered to retroactively pay his wages and bonuses, and that the legal liability of those responsible be pursued, these requests do not fall within the scope of compensation provided for by the State Compensation Law and are not supported.

Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 17, 21, 22, 33, and 35 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, the Compensation Committee of the Guangdong High People's Court decided on July 20, 2011:

1. To affirm Item 1 of the Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 of the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court;

2. To amend Item 2 of the Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 of the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court to read: The Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Court shall pay the claimant Mai Liang compensation for infringement of personal freedom in the amount of RMB 74,129.13;

3. To quash Item 3 of the Decision Letter (2010) Sui Zhong Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1 of the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court;

4. The Guangzhou Tianhe District People's Court shall, within the scope of the impact of the infringing act, eliminate the effects for the claimant Mai Liang, restore his reputation, apologize to him, and pay moral damages in the amount of RMB 50,000;

5. To dismiss the other compensation requests of the claimant Mai Liang.
